name: MCP4728T-E_UN
title: 12-bit quad voltage-output DAC with EEPROM and I2C interface
summary: Four 12-bit resistor-string DACs with buffered rail-to-rail outputs in a 10-lead MSOP, run from one 2.7 V to 5.5 V supply and controlled over I2C up to 3.4 Mbit/s. Each channel chooses the internal 2.048 V reference (gain 1 or 2) or VDD, and can be powered down to a 1 kΩ, 100 kΩ or 500 kΩ load to ground. Codes, configuration and the three I2C address bits are kept in on-chip EEPROM and reloaded at power-up, so the outputs return to their stored values without host action. An LDAC pin updates all four outputs together.
key_figures: 0 V to 2.048 V or 4.096 V (internal reference), 0 V to VDD (VREF = VDD)
800 µA typ, 1400 µA max, 4 channels on, VDD = 5.5 V
100 kHz, 400 kHz, 3.4 MHz; 8 addresses in EEPROM

notes: Ordering code: MCP4728 + address option (A0 to A7, omitted for the default 000) + T for tape and reel + -E (extended temperature, -40 °C to +125 °C) + /UN (10-lead MSOP).
The address bits set by the option are factory-programmed into EEPROM and can be rewritten by the user.

pins.name: VDD
pins.function: Supply input, 2.7 V to 5.5 V; also the external reference for any channel that selects VDD.

pins.name: SCL
pins.function: I2C clock in. The device is a slave only; needs a pull-up to VDD. Leave floating if unused.

pins.name: SDA
pins.function: I2C data in and out, open-drain; needs a pull-up to VDD. Leave floating if unused.

pins.name: LDAC
pins.function: Active-low latch: a high-to-low edge copies all four input registers to the output registers at once. Also selects the device during I2C address read and write. May be driven by an MCU.

pins.name: RDY/BSY
pins.function: Low while EEPROM is being programmed, high otherwise. Needs a pull-up of about 100 kΩ to VDD; leave floating if unused.

pins.name: VOUT A
pins.function: Channel A buffered voltage output, rail to rail.

pins.function: Channel B buffered voltage output, rail to rail.

pins.function: Channel C buffered voltage output, rail to rail.

pins.function: Channel D buffered voltage output, rail to rail.

circuits.title: Device connection
circuits.description: The DAC on an I2C bus. R1 and R2 pull SCL and SDA up to VDD; R3 pulls RDY/BSY up so a controller can watch the EEPROM busy flag. SCL, SDA, LDAC and RDY/BSY run to the microcontroller, and the four outputs leave as analog signals. C1 (ceramic) and C2 (tantalum) decouple VDD to ground.

parts.note: SCL pull-up; 5 kΩ to 10 kΩ for fSCL 100 kHz to 400 kHz, about 700 Ω at 3.4 MHz
SDA pull-up; 5 kΩ to 10 kΩ for fSCL 100 kHz to 400 kHz, about 700 Ω at 3.4 MHz
RDY/BSY pull-up; RDY/BSY may be left floating when unused

circuits.title: Set point or threshold calibration
circuits.description: Four light-sensing channels, each with a photodiode from VDD into a sense resistor that feeds a comparator's inverting input. Each DAC channel sets that comparator's trip level through an R1/R2 divider with a 0.1 µF capacitor across R2: VOUT D drives comparator 1, VOUT C comparator 2, VOUT B comparator 3 and VOUT A comparator 4. The bus side matches the basic connection: pull-ups on SCL, SDA and RDY/BSY, LDAC to the MCU, and 0.1 µF plus 10 µF on VDD.
notes: VTRIP = VOUT × R2 / (R1 + R2), with VOUT = VREF × Dn / 4096 × Gx and Dn from 0 to 4095.
Misprint: the SDA pull-up is marked both R2 and R3; it is one resistor, R2.

operation.text: Four independent 12-bit resistor-string DACs, each followed by a low-power rail-to-rail buffer amplifier with gain 1 or 2. Every channel has a volatile input register, an output register and its own EEPROM copy of configuration and code. An on-chip charge pump makes the EEPROM programming voltage.

Each channel picks its own reference with its VREF bit: the internal 2.048 V reference or VDD. The internal reference runs as long as at least one channel uses it and shuts off when all four select VDD. With VDD as reference, supply noise appears directly on the output, so the supply has to be clean. Gain 2 is available only with the internal reference.

A POR circuit watches VDD. Below the threshold everything is disabled and there is no output. Above it the device resets and loads each channel's EEPROM contents into both its input and output registers, so the outputs come up at the stored settings with no need for LDAC or UDAC. The POR bit in a read shows the state.

A general call with second byte 06h acts like a POR: the current conversion is dropped, EEPROM data goes into all input and output registers at the ACK, and the outputs change without regard to LDAC. Power-down bits are taken from EEPROM too.
As shipped: address bits 000 (unless an address option was ordered), VREF = internal on all channels, normal mode, gain 1, code 000h.

The output registers change on: LDAC going low (all channels); UDAC = 0 in a write (that channel only); the general call software update, 08h (all channels); and POR or general call reset (all channels, from EEPROM). With LDAC held low, each register reaches the output at the ACK of the last data byte. The fast write ignores UDAC. LDAC must stay low at least 210 ns.

The buffer swings rail to rail and can deliver a load current of up to 24 mA. It stays stable driving 1000 pF together with 5 kΩ. Loads above 5 kΩ are the recommended range. Output DC impedance in normal mode is about 1 Ω.

Each channel enters power-down through its PD1, PD0 bits. The channel's circuits mostly switch off and its output pin is tied to ground through 1 kΩ, 100 kΩ or 500 kΩ. Register and EEPROM contents stay as they were; the I2C interface keeps listening, and the internal reference stays on if any channel uses it. With all four channels down and VDD as reference the device draws about 40 nA. The lowest consumption therefore comes from selecting VDD as reference on all channels first, then powering all down; unused channels are best kept powered down.

Any write that sets normal mode wakes the addressed channel; general call wake-up (09h) clears PD1, PD0 on all channels; general call reset wakes channels according to their EEPROM power-down bits. The output appears about 4.5 µs after the ACK of the command, a delay that is in addition to the settling time.

Sequential write, single write and address write program EEPROM, starting at the falling edge of the last ACK. RDY/BSY (pin and bit) goes low for the write, typically 25 ms and at most 50 ms, and commands sent meanwhile are ignored. Data are retained 200 years at +25 °C.

Slave only, two-wire, standard (100 kbit/s), fast (400 kbit/s) and high speed (3.4 Mbit/s). Data are taken on rising SCL edges and driven out on falling edges. The address byte is device code 1100, then A2 A1 A0, then R/W, giving eight addresses on one bus. High speed is entered with the master code 00001XXX, which the device does not acknowledge, and lasts until the next stop. A device on the bus can be found by sending its address and checking for an ACK.
A first byte of 00h (general call) is answered with an ACK, and the second byte picks the action: 06h reset, 09h wake-up, 08h software update, 0Ch read address bits.

The address bits live in EEPROM and are reported by the general call read address command, which needs LDAC to fall during the low phase of the 8th clock of the second byte and remain low until the third byte is done; the device returns its EEPROM and register address bits. The write address command needs the current address and the same LDAC sequence, sends the new address twice, programs EEPROM after the fourth byte and takes effect after the stop. Without the LDAC sequence the third byte is not acknowledged. Both commands run at 400 kHz at most; LDAC returns to its normal role after the stop.

Neither offset nor gain is trimmed in production. The bulk of gain error is due to the output buffer saturating at codes above about 4000; using codes 100 to 4000 gives a more linear transfer and is the route to gain error under 1 %. Both errors can be corrected in software.
Settling time is taken to 0.5 LSB of the final value for a code step from 400h to C00h.
Bypass VDD with about 0.1 µF ceramic to ground, plus 10 µF tantalum in parallel for high-frequency noise, both within 4 mm of the VDD pin.

SCL, SDA and RDY/BSY are open drain. SCL and SDA pull-ups are typically 5 kΩ to 10 kΩ at 100 kHz to 400 kHz and below 1 kΩ (about 700 Ω) at 3.4 MHz; larger values save power but slow the edges, and a heavily loaded bus needs smaller values. RDY/BSY takes about 100 kΩ.

A multilayer board with a low-inductance ground plane, isolated inputs and outputs and good decoupling is needed for best results. With separate digital and analog grounds, VSS and the ground ends of the VDD capacitors go to the analog plane, and VDD and VSS sit on the analog supply plane.
